title: Clinical thresholds for haemorrhage classes and dehydration severity
source: ATLS haemorrhage classes as transcribed by Tom Wade MD from the ATLS 9th edition Student Course Manual (a secondary page; the manual itself was not opened); dehydration bands from an AAFP summary of Steiner et al., JAMA 2004;291:2746-54 (children). No clinical source found for organ-function floors.
rows: Haemorrhage class I: blood volume lost
70 kg adult trauma patient; up to 750 mL
Heart rate under 100, systolic pressure normal, pulse pressure normal, respiratory rate 14 to 20, urine over 30 mL/h, slightly anxious.
Haemorrhage class II: blood volume lost
Heart rate 100 to 120, systolic normal, pulse pressure decreased, respiratory rate 20 to 30, urine 20 to 30 mL/h, mildly anxious.
Haemorrhage class III: blood volume lost
Heart rate 120 to 140, systolic decreased, pulse pressure decreased, respiratory rate 30 to 40, urine 5 to 15 mL/h, anxious or confused.
Haemorrhage class IV: blood volume lost
Heart rate over 140, systolic decreased, pulse pressure decreased, respiratory rate over 35, urine negligible, confused or lethargic.
Children; 'most guidelines' per the AAFP summary of Steiner 2004
For under 2s other sources give 5/10/15%; those pages were not opened.
Organ-function floors (a level below which an organ stops)
